header: IN THE HIGH COURT OF SINDH BENCH AT SUKKUR
(Muhammad Moosa v. P.O Sindh and others)
For Petitioner : None present for the petitioner
For Respondents : M/s Ali Raza Balouch & Israr Ahmed
body: Andan Iqbal Chaudhry J.- The petitioner had applied for the post of Police Constable in the Sindh Police on the Deceased Quota and was recommended for appointment. However, upon the requisite medical screening test, he tested “HBs Ag reactive”, i.e., prone to Hepatitis “B”. He was therefore declared unfit and his selection was withdrawn.

It is stated that the petitioner subsequently got himself rescreened at the Aga Khan University Hospital, where the result was negative. He prays for a writ directing that another medical screening test of the petitioner be conducted by the respondents. The recruitment process for the year 2024, during which the petitioner tested “HBs Ag reactive”, has since been concluded. We are not inclined to re-open the recruitment process by way of another medical screening test for the petitioner, inasmuch as that would be discriminatory towards the other candidates who had been rejected on the same ground. However, since the petitioner had been recommended for appointment on the Deceased Quota, he will be free to apply afresh as and when fresh vacancies are advertised. The medical screening test at that time would determine whether he is fit or not. With that observation, the petition is dismissed.
J U D G E J U D G E M.Ali*
